title: a seal over stale CRLF bytes is refused, naming the file
intention: No seal lands over a closure file whose working bytes are not what checking out its index blob would write today while git calls it unchanged; the seal door refuses naming the file, so a seal on every box is the fingerprint of the committed bytes.
why: Measured 2026-11-13: the Windows seal of cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_flock_stands_for_fcntl.py at 52890c2f8 carries fp 133032682e11; Linux hashes 8318d78f2eda over the same 3-file closure. Brute force over every version of each file x CRLF per file finds one match: the committed bytes with cairn/tools/base/__init__.py alone in CRLF. That file last changed 2026-08-13; the *.py eol=lf pin (88e30cde9bd4) landed 2026-11-12 19:04, and git rewrites a working file under a new attribute only when it writes it again. git status reads such a tree clean, so the hook's hold and stage seal and commit it; the Linux hook reseal then dropped 5a37's hollow reading over the skewed seal.
traces_to: Law 3 - a seal is a measurement of named bytes, and one whose bytes differ per box is not one measurement; Law 8 - a Windows green that cannot reproduce on Linux is a hollow green a peer leans on.
how: A new cairn/devices/tester/working_bytes.py holds one predicate, unnormalized(files, base): candidates are tracked files whose raw hash differs from the index sha; a candidate is flagged when its cleaned hash equals the index sha and the index blob smudged for its path differs from its raw bytes. run_proof (sink=validations) refuses before persist; the reseal door refuses after its run; dirty_against_index names flagged files so the hook holds them.

clauses.claim: in a scratch repo with core.autocrlf=true whose .py was checked out before an eol=lf pin, unnormalized names that file and dirty_against_index names it, while git status reads the tree clean
an all-LF tree is named by neither, and a genuinely edited file is named by dirty_against_index but never by unnormalized
TesterDevice.run_proof with sink=validations over a proof whose closure holds a stale CRLF file raises UnnormalizedClosure naming the file and persists no validation

decisions.text: D1: cairn/devices/tester/working_bytes.py: unnormalized(files, base) -> sorted repo-relative paths, per how; UnnormalizedClosure(Exception) carrying .files; refusal_text(files) naming each file and the one-time fix (git rm --cached -r -q . && git reset --hard on a clean tree). Regular files only (mode 100644/100755); untracked, symlink and gitlink entries are skipped.

D2: device.run_proof: when sink == validations and the closure was read (not the directory fallback), unnormalized(closure, validation_store._REPO_ROOT); non-empty -> persist nothing, raise UnnormalizedClosure. cli.py --seal catches it into the refused lane (SEAL REFUSED prints its text).

D3: reseal.py: dirty_against_index appends unnormalized(files, base), so the hook (index_only) holds the seal before running and stage_clean_seals never stages one; reseal() after its run raises ResealRefused(refusal_text) when the record's closure holds a flagged file.

D4: the proof builds scratch git repos (scratch_dir) with core.autocrlf=true, commits before and after the pin, and never touches the live tree; tooth 3 repoints validation_store._REPO_ROOT at the scratch repo for one run_proof; one tooth per clause.
